title: ACS handler should validate against response Issuer, not first IdP
description:
## Problem

When handling SAML responses at the ACS endpoint, `handleACSForSP` always validates against the first IdP in the metadata store (`idps[0]`), regardless of which IdP actually sent the response.

**Location**: `internal/adapters/driving/caddy/plugin.go:2069-2079`

```go
// For Phase 1 with single IdP, get the first IdP from metadata store
idps, err := spConfig.metadataStore.ListIdPs("")
...
idp := &idps[0]  // <-- ALWAYS uses first IdP!
```

## Symptom

When multiple IdPs are configured:
1. User selects IdP A from discovery page
2. User authenticates at IdP A
3. IdP A sends SAML response back to ACS
4. ACS validates response against IdP B (first in list)
5. Validation fails: "response Issuer does not match the IDP metadata"

## Solution

1. Parse the SAML response to extract the Issuer element
2. Look up the matching IdP from the metadata store by entity ID
3. Validate the response against that IdP

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ACS handler extracts Issuer from SAML response before validation
- [ ] ACS handler looks up IdP by Issuer entity ID
- [ ] Returns clear error if Issuer IdP not found in metadata
- [ ] Works correctly with multiple IdPs configured
close_reason: Fixed: ACS handler now extracts Issuer from SAML response and looks up IdP by entity ID

title: redirectToIdP should show discovery page when multiple IdPs are configured
description:
Problem: When an unauthenticated user visits a protected resource and multiple IdPs are configured via `idp_filter`, the `redirectToIdPForSP` function always redirects to the first IdP in the list instead of showing the discovery page. This defeats the purpose of having multiple IdPs configured.

Location: 
- `internal/adapters/driving/caddy/plugin.go` lines 2582-2588 (`redirectToIdPForSP`)
- `internal/adapters/driving/caddy/plugin.go` lines 638-644 (`redirectToIdP`)

Current behavior:
```go
idps, err := spConfig.metadataStore.ListIdPs("")
if err != nil || len(idps) == 0 {
    s.renderAppError(w, r, domain.ConfigError("No identity provider is configured"))
    return
}
idp := &idps[0]  // Always uses first IdP regardless of count
```

Expected behavior:
When `len(idps) > 1`, redirect to the discovery page (`/saml/disco`) with the return URL as a query parameter, so the user can choose their IdP.

Proposed fix:
```go
if len(idps) > 1 {
    // Redirect to discovery page when multiple IdPs available
    redirectURL := "/saml/disco?return_url=" + url.QueryEscape(r.URL.RequestURI())
    http.Redirect(w, r, redirectURL, http.StatusFound)
    return
}
// Single IdP - redirect directly
idp := &idps[0]
```

Affected functions:
1. `redirectToIdP` (single-SP mode)
2. `redirectToIdPForSP` (multi-SP mode)

Workaround: Users can set `login_redirect /saml/disco` in the Caddyfile to force discovery page usage.
close_reason: Implemented multi-IdP redirect to discovery page in both redirectToIdP (single-SP) and redirectToIdPForSP (multi-SP) functions. When len(idps) > 1, redirects to /saml/disco?return_url=... instead of always using the first IdP.

title: IdP Filter Comma-Separated Pattern Support
description:
## Problem

`idp_filter` does not support comma-separated patterns, while the other filters do:
- `registration_authority_filter` ✅ comma-separated
- `entity_category_filter` ✅ comma-separated  
- `assurance_certification_filter` ✅ comma-separated
- `idp_filter` ❌ single pattern only

This inconsistency prevents filtering to specific IdPs like:
```
idp_filter *uni-mannheim.de*,*uni-heidelberg.de*
```

## Solution

Add comma-separated parsing to `filterIdPs()` matching the pattern used by other filters:
```go
patterns := strings.Split(pattern, ",")
for i := range patterns {
    patterns[i] = strings.TrimSpace(patterns[i])
}
```

## Files
- `internal/adapters/driven/metadata/file.go` - `filterIdPs()` function (line ~279)
- `internal/core/domain/metadata.go` - `MatchesEntityIDPattern()` (no change needed)
- `internal/adapters/driven/metadata/options.go` - Update docstring for `WithIdPFilter`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `idp_filter *a*,*b*` matches IdPs containing "a" OR "b"
- [ ] Whitespace around commas is trimmed
- [ ] Empty patterns after split are ignored
- [ ] Existing single-pattern behavior unchanged
- [ ] Unit tests cover comma-separated patterns

title: Refactor caddyfile.go to eliminate directive parsing duplication
description:
The Caddyfile parsing in `internal/adapters/driving/caddy/caddyfile.go` has significant code duplication:

## Problem

- `UnmarshalCaddyfile()` (lines 46-373) parses directives into `s.Config` for single-SP mode
- `parseSPConfigField()` (lines 376-673) parses identical directives into `spCfg.Config` for multi-SP mode
- ~35 directive handlers are duplicated between these functions
- Violates DRY principle and creates maintenance hazards (changes must be made in two places)

## Solution

Extract a shared `parseDirective(d *caddyfile.Dispenser, cfg *Config)` function that both parsers call.

## Additional improvements

- Add early EntityID validation at parse time (call domain.ValidateEntityID)
- Consolidate header validation to Config.Validate() only (remove from parser)

## Impact

- Reduces lines of code by ~200-250
- Makes future directive changes atomic (single implementation)
- Improves code maintainability
close_reason: Refactored caddyfile.go to eliminate directive parsing duplication. Created shared parseConfigDirective() function that reduces file from 673 to 393 lines (42% reduction). Added EntityID validation at parse time. Removed duplicate header validation from parser (kept in Config.Validate()). All caddyfile tests pass.

title: Break down plugin.go god file (2787 lines)
description:
## Problem

`internal/adapters/driving/caddy/plugin.go` is a god file at 2787 lines with 50+ methods. It violates single responsibility principle - changes for unrelated reasons.

## Already Extracted

- `cookies.go` (160 lines) - Cookie management
- `urls.go` (95 lines) - URL resolution

## Remaining Extraction Candidates

| Category | Methods | Est. Lines |
|----------|---------|------------|
| **Rendering** | `renderDiscoveryHTML`, `renderHTTPError`, `renderAppError`, `handleDenied` + ForSP variants | ~90 |
| **Attribute Headers** | `applyAttributeHeaders`, `shouldStripAttributeHeaders` + ForSP variants | ~100 |
| **Setters** | `SetMetadataStore`, `SetSAMLService`, etc. | ~50 |
| **Handler duplication** | `handleX` + `handleXForSP` patterns could share code | Major refactor |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] plugin.go under 2000 lines
- [ ] Each extracted file has single clear responsibility
- [ ] All tests pass after each extraction
close_reason: Plugin.go reduced from 2787 to 1659 lines. Extracted rendering.go, headers.go, handlers_sp.go
